title: GCP Cloud Functions Memory Utilization

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `google:gcp:monitoring` events with `metric.type="cloudfunctions.googleapis.com/function/user_memory_bytes"` into `index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.5.7 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `google:gcp:monitoring` traffic without `metric.type="cloudfunctions.googleapis.com/function/user_memory_bytes"`. Confirm UC-4.5.7 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:monitoring` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" metric.type="cloudfunctions.googleapis.com/function/user_memory_bytes"
| table _time resource.type metric.type value
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.7_gcp_cloud_functions_memo_7"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.5.7 — GCP Cloud Functions Memory Utilization: queries Google Cloud `google:gcp:monitoring` for search criteria `metric.type="cloudfunctions.googleapis.com/function/user_memory_bytes"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On Google Cloud, detecting 'GCP Cloud Functions Memory Utilization' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.5.7 drives medium-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Export Cloud Monitoring metrics for Cloud Functions to Splunk via the GCP add-on. Join max memory usage with deployed memory configuration from labels or an asset lookup. Alert when utilization consistently approaches the configured limit (for example >85% of allocated memory).
visualization: Line chart (avg/max memory by function), Gauge (peak vs allocation), Table (function_name, max_mb, allocation_mb).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.mem_used_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.Memory
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (Memory node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:monitoring`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `resource.type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Export Cloud Monitoring metrics for Cloud Functions to Splunk via the GCP add-on. Join max memory usage with deployed memory configuration from labels or an asset lookup. Alert when utilization consistently approaches the configured limit (for example >85% of allocated memory).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" metric.type="cloudfunctions.googleapis.com/function/user_memory_bytes"
| table _time resource.type metric.type value
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.7_gcp_cloud_functions_memo_7"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:monitoring` in `index=gcp` to detect gcp cloud functions memory utilization. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `resource.type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_7_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (avg/max memory by function), Gauge (peak vs allocation), Table (function_name, max_mb, allocation_mb)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of gcp cloud functions memory utilization so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
